causes.short: a hidden flaw in a weld
causes.finding: A weld in one of the {component}'s propellant lines had a void inside it that no surface check could see. Under load it cracked, and the leak starved the engine.
causes.fix: Every weld on the propellant lines is now X-rayed, not only a sample from each batch.

causes.finding: A cable bundle in the {component} had rubbed against the edge of a bracket under vibration until its insulation wore through, and the bare wire shorted a control circuit.
causes.fix: The bundles are now sleeved and clamped clear of sharp edges, and the bracket was redrawn with a rounded lip.

causes.finding: A shred of cleaning cloth left inside a propellant valve during assembly kept the valve from seating.
causes.fix: Assembly now ends with the whole system flushed and filtered, and every open port is capped and logged until it is closed for good.

causes.finding: A batch of fasteners from one supplier was softer than its specification, and one of them sheared under the load of flight.
causes.fix: Fasteners from every batch are now tested on arrival, and the supplier's own batch records are audited.

causes.finding: A liquid oxygen fill valve on the {component} iced up partly open, and the tank pressure it let fall could not be brought back in time.
causes.fix: The valve now has a heater and a second position sensor, and the count can hold and recover instead of scrubbing.

causes.finding: An umbilical plug came out of its socket a moment early, and the {component} lost ground power before its own batteries had taken over.
causes.fix: The switch to internal power now comes first and must be confirmed before any plug is released.

causes.short: a pressure sensor out of calibration
causes.finding: A tank pressure sensor on the {component} had drifted out of calibration and reported a fault that wasn't there. The safety logic did exactly what it was told and stopped the count.
causes.fix: Critical readings now come from two sensors each, and a disagreement between them holds the count instead of ending it.

causes.finding: Rain in the days before the launch had worked its way into a connector at the base of the {component}, and the moisture caused a short that came and went.
causes.fix: Connectors on the pad are now sealed against the weather, and a dry-nitrogen purge runs through them for the whole countdown.

causes.finding: A bearing in the {component}'s turbopump overheated and seized seconds into the flight. Without the pump the engine lost its thrust.
causes.fix: The bearing has a new cage design and more coolant flowing through it, and every pump now runs a longer acceptance test.

causes.finding: The pressure in one of the {component}'s combustion chambers began to swing back and forth hundreds of times a second, and the shaking tore the injector apart.
causes.fix: Baffles across the injector face now break up the oscillation; the change was proven on the test stand by setting off small charges inside a running chamber.

causes.finding: The {component} began to bounce along its length as its thrust and the flow of its propellant fed each other, until the shaking broke a line.
causes.fix: Gas-filled accumulators in the feed lines now soak up the pressure waves before they can build.

causes.finding: A gyroscope in the {component}'s guidance platform drifted, and the vehicle steered steadily away from its planned path.
causes.fix: The gyroscopes now run in for longer before they are installed, and a second platform checks the first.

causes.short: a skin panel thinner than its drawings
causes.finding: The {component} broke up as it passed through the moment of greatest air pressure. One of its skin panels had been milled thinner than its drawings called for.
causes.fix: Panels are now measured after milling, and the flight path was reshaped to ease the peak load.

causes.finding: A leaking hydraulic line drained the actuators that swivel the {component}'s engines, and without steering the vehicle tumbled.
causes.fix: The line has a new fitting with a locking collar, and the system now carries a reserve.

causes.short: an upper stage that lit too soon
causes.finding: The {component}'s upper stage lit while the spent stage was still attached below it, and its exhaust had nowhere to go.
causes.fix: Staging now waits for a confirmed separation signal, not a timer alone.

causes.short: an explosive bolt that did not fire
causes.finding: One of the explosive bolts holding the {component}'s stages together did not fire, and the stack was dragged off course by what it could not let go of.
causes.fix: Every bolt now has two igniters on separate circuits.

causes.short: a nose shroud that stayed latched
causes.finding: One half of the {component}'s nose shroud stayed latched, and the payload could not get clear of it.
causes.fix: The latches were redesigned with springs that push each half away, and the release is now tested on every shroud.

causes.finding: The separation springs released unevenly and set the payload tumbling faster than its own controls could stop.
causes.fix: The springs are now matched in sets, and each release is filmed on the test rig.

causes.short: propellant that floated away from the outlets
causes.finding: The {component}'s upper stage did not relight after its coast: in weightlessness its propellant had drifted away from the tank outlets.
causes.fix: Small settling rockets now push the propellant back over the outlets before every restart.

causes.finding: Sunlight warmed the {component}'s upper-stage tanks more than predicted during the coast, and the propellant that boiled off left too little for the burn.
causes.fix: Better insulation and a new attitude for the coast now keep the tanks in shade.

causes.finding: A faulty level sensor told the {component}'s engine that its tank was empty while propellant remained, and the engine shut down short of the planned speed.
causes.fix: Shutdown now needs two sensors to agree.

causes.finding: A helium bottle that keeps the {component}'s tanks pressurized leaked slowly through a fitting, and by the time of the burn the pressure had fallen too far.
causes.fix: The fittings are now brazed rather than threaded, and the pressure is checked again before each burn.

causes.finding: A solder joint on one of the {component}'s circuit boards cracked as it heated and cooled, and the system it fed went silent.
causes.fix: Boards are now cycled through heat and cold many more times before they fly.

causes.short: an error in the stored command sequence
causes.finding: One command in the {component}'s stored sequence carried the wrong value, and the craft followed it faithfully.
causes.fix: Every command list is now checked by a second team against a simulation of the whole flight.

causes.finding: A charged particle flipped a bit in the {component}'s memory, and the craft took the corrupted value for an order.
causes.fix: Critical values are now kept in three copies, and the craft goes by the majority.

causes.short: a battery damaged on the pad
causes.finding: The {component}'s battery overheated while it charged on the pad, and the cells it damaged could no longer carry the load.
causes.fix: Charging now runs at a lower rate, with a temperature cutoff.

causes.short: a connector mated one pin out of line
causes.finding: A connector on the {component} had been mated one pin out of line. The checkout had tested the circuit at the box, not through the cable.
causes.fix: Checkout now tests every circuit end to end, through the flight cables.

causes.short: a bracket that resonated with the rocket
causes.finding: A bracket inside the {component} resonated with the rocket's vibration and broke, and the unit it held came loose.
causes.fix: The bracket was stiffened, and the craft is now shaken to the full launch levels before it ships.

causes.short: air trapped in a sealed compartment
causes.finding: Air trapped in a sealed compartment of the {component} could not escape fast enough as the rocket climbed, and the pressure burst a panel.
causes.fix: Every compartment now has a vent sized for the climb.

causes.finding: The roar of liftoff shook the {component}'s thin antenna dish until it cracked.
causes.fix: The dish now has stiffening ribs, and the craft is tested in an acoustic chamber.

causes.short: a boom that jammed on its hinge
causes.finding: A folded boom on the {component} jammed on its hinge, and with it folded the craft could not point.
causes.fix: The hinge has more clearance and a stronger spring, and deployment is tested hot and cold.

causes.short: a solar panel that did not unfold
causes.finding: A solar panel's restraint cable on the {component} did not cut, and without the panel the craft ran down its batteries.
causes.fix: Each restraint cable now has two cutters.

causes.finding: The {component} came away spinning faster than it was built for, and the force tore at its booms and antennas.
causes.fix: The spin rockets were resized and their timing checked again on the ground.

causes.finding: The {component} ran hotter in sunlight than its designers predicted, and its electronics went past their limits.
causes.fix: More of its surface is now covered with reflective tape, and its electronics are rated for higher temperatures.

causes.finding: The sensor that finds the Sun lost its lock, and the {component} spent its control gas hunting for it.
causes.fix: A second sensor, and a limit on the gas a search may use, now keep a lost craft from emptying its tanks.

causes.finding: The {component}'s transmitter tube failed under the strain of a long flight, and nothing more was heard.
causes.fix: A spare transmitter now flies on every craft, switched in automatically.

causes.short: an engine valve slow to close
causes.finding: The {component}'s engine burned longer than ordered: a valve was slow to close.
causes.fix: The valve now closes on two signals, and a separate timer cuts every burn off as well.

causes.short: a short that took down the power
causes.finding: A short in one instrument pulled the {component}'s whole power supply down, because nothing isolated it.
causes.fix: Each instrument now sits behind its own fuse.

causes.short: a heat shield that wore away too fast
causes.finding: The {component}'s heat shield wore away faster than tests had shown, and the instruments inside overheated before the parachute opened.
causes.fix: The shield is now thicker, and its material was tested again at the speeds of a real entry.

causes.finding: The {component}'s parachute opened at a speed it was not built for, and tore.
causes.fix: Deployment now waits for a lower speed, and the canopy was reinforced.

causes.short: a hull that gave way to the pressure
causes.finding: The {component}'s hull gave way to an atmosphere denser than its design assumed.
causes.fix: The design now assumes the harshest measurement on record, not the average, and is tested in a pressure chamber beyond it.

causes.finding: The {component}'s radar altimeter mistook a stray echo for the surface, and the braking came too late.
causes.fix: The altimeter now checks two beams against each other before it trusts a reading.

causes.finding: The insulation of a wire bundle behind a panel in the {component} had been nicked during assembly, and in flight the bare wire shorted.
causes.fix: Wiring is now inspected after every panel is closed, and the bundles run behind guards.

causes.short: a damaged switch in an oxygen tank
causes.finding: A heater switch inside an oxygen tank of the {component} had been damaged in a ground test long before the flight. In flight it overheated, and the tank failed.
causes.fix: The switches are now rated for the voltage they really see, and tank tests record the temperature inside the tank.

causes.finding: Coolant leaked from a fitting in the {component}'s cooling loop, and without it the electronics overheated.
causes.fix: The loop's fittings are now brazed, and the loop is leak-tested under pressure before every launch.

causes.short: a hatch seal that failed its check
causes.finding: The {component}'s hatch seal failed its pressure check in the countdown, and the flight could not go on with a cabin that might leak.
causes.fix: The seal is made of a new material, and its check now comes earlier, while there is time to fix it.

causes.finding: A spark from a wire found materials in the {component}'s cabin that burned far more fiercely than anyone had expected.
causes.fix: Every cabin material is now tested for how it burns, and the cabin is no longer filled with pure oxygen on the pad.

causes.short: a cabin vent that stuck open
causes.finding: A cabin vent in the {component} failed to close as it climbed, and the cabin pressure fell.
causes.fix: The vent now closes on a spring, and its closing is checked on the pad.

causes.finding: Insulation shed by the rocket struck the {component} during the climb and damaged its skin.
causes.fix: The insulation that could shed was bonded again, and cameras now watch every climb.

causes.finding: The joint between the {component} and its adapter flexed beyond its design load under the climb's acceleration, and cracked.
causes.fix: The joint was strengthened and load-tested to half again beyond what a flight puts on it.

causes.finding: The {component}'s docking latches did not engage: a guide had bent on first contact and held them out of line.
causes.fix: The guides are stiffer, and the latches were tested again across the whole range of approach angles.

causes.finding: One of the {component}'s attitude thrusters stuck open and set the craft spinning.
causes.fix: Each ring of thrusters can now be shut off on its own, and the valves were redesigned.

causes.short: separation charges that fired out of order
causes.finding: A separation charge on the {component} fired out of order and damaged the module beside it.
causes.fix: The firing circuits are now interlocked, so the charges can only fire in sequence.

causes.short: a rendezvous radar that lost its target
causes.finding: The {component}'s rendezvous radar lost its target at close range, and the approach went on without the numbers it needed.
causes.fix: The radar's antenna mount was changed to keep the target in view, and the approach now has a fallback using optical tracking.

causes.short: carbon dioxide absorbent spoiled by damp
causes.finding: The {component}'s carbon dioxide cartridges saturated far faster than rated: their absorbent had taken up moisture in storage.
causes.fix: Cartridges are now sealed for storage, and some from every batch are tested.

causes.finding: A fuel cell in the {component} flooded with its own water, and its output collapsed.
causes.fix: The water separator was redesigned, and the cells now have a backup battery.

causes.finding: The {component}'s guidance computer was flooded with data it did not need, and dropped tasks it did.
causes.fix: The program now sheds its least important work first, and the switch that fed the extra data was rewired.

causes.short: radiators too small for the attitude
causes.finding: The {component}'s radiators could not shed enough heat in the attitude it held, and the cabin warmed beyond its limits.
causes.fix: Flight plans now turn the craft to spread the sunlight evenly, and the radiators were enlarged.

causes.short: a pressure valve that opened early
causes.finding: A pressure-equalizing valve in the {component} opened before its time, and the cabin lost its air.
causes.fix: The valve was redesigned so that it cannot open while the cabin is sealed, and it has a cover that can be closed by hand.

causes.short: a seam in the heat shield
causes.finding: A seam in the {component}'s heat shield opened under the heat of reentry.
causes.fix: The shield's seams are now bonded in a single cure and inspected with ultrasound.

causes.short: a parachute tangled in its lines
causes.finding: The {component}'s main parachute tangled in its own lines as it came out.
causes.fix: The packing method was changed, and the chute now opens in stages.

causes.finding: The {component}'s retrorocket burned for less than its planned time, and the craft met the atmosphere at the wrong angle.
causes.fix: The burn now has a second, independent timer, and the engine controller a backup.

causes.finding: The {component}'s equipment module did not fully separate before reentry, and the two entered the atmosphere still joined.
causes.fix: The separation bolts now have twin charges, and the straps that held were redesigned to cut cleanly.

causes.short: landing rockets that fired too late
causes.finding: The {component}'s landing rockets fired too late to soften the impact: their trigger had been confused by the swaying of the parachute.
causes.fix: The trigger now ignores readings it cannot confirm, and the rockets have a backup timer.

causes.short: a hatch hinge bent in vacuum
causes.finding: The {component}'s hatch would not seal again after the spacewalk: its hinge had bent as it opened in vacuum.
causes.fix: The hinge is stronger, and the hatch is now tested opening and closing in a vacuum chamber.

causes.finding: The {component}'s airlock valve leaked as it filled again, and the craft could not hold its air.
causes.fix: The valve now seats against two seals, and checking both is part of the airlock procedure.

causes.finding: A seam in a glove of the {component} split at the knuckle, where it flexes with every grip.
causes.fix: The glove is now stitched in a different pattern and flexed thousands of times on a test rig before it flies.

causes.finding: The pump of the {component}'s cooling garment stalled, and the suit overheated within minutes.
causes.fix: The pump has a backup, and the suit now warns early of a rise in temperature.

causes.finding: The {component}'s oxygen regulator froze in the cold of shadow and gave too little flow.
causes.fix: The regulator now has a heater and was tested again at the coldest temperatures of a spacewalk.

causes.short: a suit too stiff to work in
causes.finding: Pressurized in vacuum, the {component} was far stiffer than in tests on the ground, and the work planned for it could not be done.
causes.fix: Joints with bearings now let the suit bend under pressure, and the work plan adds handholds and rests.

causes.finding: A tether clip on the {component} opened under a load it should have held.
causes.fix: The clip was redesigned to lock, and every tether is now load-tested before flight.

causes.finding: The {component}'s visor fogged over, and the work outside had to stop.
causes.fix: The visor has an anti-fog coating, and more air now flows across it.

causes.finding: The {component}'s umbilical kinked and cut off the flow of oxygen to the suit.
causes.fix: The umbilical now has a stiffer sleeve that cannot bend tightly enough to close.

causes.short: a sharp edge on the craft
causes.finding: A sharp edge on the outside of the craft cut through the {component}'s outer layers.
causes.fix: Edges along every route outside are now padded, and the suit's outer layer is thicker at the knees and hands.

causes.short: a fuel leak that caught fire
causes.finding: Kerosene leaking from a loose fitting on the {component} pooled at the foot of the pad, and a spark from the pad's electrics set it alight.
causes.fix: Every fitting is now leak-checked under pressure before fuelling, and the pad's electrics are sealed so they cannot spark.

causes.short: an engine that lit on the pad
causes.finding: A check of the {component}'s circuits during the countdown sent a start command that should have been blocked, and an engine lit on the pad.
causes.fix: An engine can now start only through a hardware interlock that the launch sequence alone releases, and circuit checks are finished before any propellant is loaded.

causes.finding: The {component}'s cameras lost their power minutes before the end, and the pictures it was sent for never came.
causes.fix: The cameras now have their own battery and switch on early, with a timer as a backup.

causes.short: a descent engine that wouldn't throttle
causes.finding: A valve in the {component}'s descent engine stuck, so the engine would not throttle down smoothly, and the craft came down faster than it could correct.
causes.fix: The valve was redesigned, and the engine's throttling is now tested across its whole range in a vacuum chamber.

causes.short: a landing radar that lost the ground
causes.finding: The {component}'s landing radar lost its lock on the surface in the last minute of the descent, and the guidance flew on old numbers.
causes.fix: The radar's antenna was moved where the craft's own legs and exhaust cannot block it, and the guidance now holds a safe hover while the radar is out.

causes.finding: Propellant sloshing in the {component}'s tanks during the descent fooled its gauges into reading them nearly empty, and the abort that followed came too late.
causes.fix: Baffles now calm the propellant, and the gauges average their readings before they warn.

causes.finding: One of the {component}'s landing legs buckled on a boulder it came down on, and the craft tipped over.
causes.fix: The legs were strengthened and their crushable struts lengthened, and landing sites must now be flatter.

causes.short: an ascent engine valve that stuck
causes.finding: One of the propellant valves of the {component}'s ascent engine opened only part of the way, and the engine never reached full thrust.
causes.fix: Each valve now has a second, parallel path, and each is fired many times on the ground before it flies.

causes.short: a stage that wouldn't let go
causes.finding: A bolt joining the {component}'s ascent stage to the stage below did not fire cleanly, and the liftoff began with the craft still held at one corner.
causes.fix: Every bolt now has two charges, and the circuits that fire them were rewired apart from each other.

causes.finding: Dust kicked up on the surface worked into a connector on the {component} and broke a circuit the liftoff needed.
causes.fix: Exposed connectors now wear dust caps that stay on until the moment they are used.

causes.finding: An actuator that moves one of the {component}'s control surfaces jammed at speed, and the craft rolled further than the other surfaces could hold.
causes.fix: The actuator now has a second motor, and its linkage was rebuilt with more room for the heat.

causes.short: a skin panel buckled by heat
causes.finding: Air friction at top speed heated a skin panel on the {component} beyond its rating, and it buckled and tore away.
causes.fix: The panel is now made of a heat-resistant alloy, and its joints let it expand.

causes.finding: The {component}'s rocket engine lit roughly, with a pressure spike that damaged its chamber.
causes.fix: The igniter was redesigned to light the propellants more evenly, and the start now pauses to check the pressures.

causes.short: a landing gear that didn't lock
causes.finding: The {component}'s landing gear collapsed as it touched down: a lock had not engaged.
causes.fix: Each gear leg now signals when it is locked, and the lock was redesigned to engage under load.

factors.text: The board found that the pressure of the schedule had pushed testing into the weeks before the flight, leaving no time to follow up on what the tests showed.
Ground tests had never put the part under the conditions it met in flight.
Inspection had checked a sample from each batch of parts, not every one.
A change to the design had reached the drawings but not everyone who built and tested the part.
Earlier flights had shown signs of the problem, and they had been filed as within limits rather than understood.
The agency had relied on its supplier's tests without checking them.
Concerns raised by engineers had not reached the people who decided whether to fly.
The design's safety margins had been worn away by weight savings made late in its development.

boardStories.headline: Board names cause of {program} loss
boardStories.lead: The independent board that investigated the loss of {mission} in {season} has published its report.
boardStories.close: {agency} has accepted every one of the board's recommendations. Its crewed flights may fly again.

boardStories.headline: {program}: what went wrong
boardStories.lead: The board of inquiry into the loss of {mission} in {season} has given its findings.
boardStories.close: The report closes with the names of the crew: {crew}.

boardStories.headline: Inquiry ends: the {program} accident explained
boardStories.deck: The board finds {cause} and calls for changes across the program
boardStories.lead: The inquiry into the loss of {mission} in {season} is over.
boardStories.close: {agency} says the changes are made, and that it will fly again.

boardStories.headline: {agency} to fly again after {program} findings
boardStories.lead: The board investigating {mission}, lost in {season}, has delivered its report.
boardStories.close: With the report published, {agency}'s crewed flights may resume.
